Verified Municipal Source: City of San Marcos, Texas

Ordinances are enforced by San Marcos Park Rangers and San Marcos Police Department. Access official municipal codes, interactive Go Zone maps, and park regulations below.

🌐 San Marcos River Rules & Container Ban ↗ 🏞️ City Parks Directory ↗
🚫 STRICTLY PROHIBITED ("No Zones")
  • 🥫
    No Single-Use Containers: Aluminum beer/soda cans, disposable water bottles, plastic cups, and juice pouches are banned in the river and on riverbanks.
  • 🍾
    No Glass Containers: Strictly forbidden by Texas State law and City ordinance throughout all river parks (violations carry fines up to $500).
  • 📦
    No Styrofoam: Styrofoam ice chests, beverage coolers, cups, and plates are strictly prohibited.
  • 🔊
    No Amplified Sound >50 Feet: Keep music volume respectful to fellow floaters and river wildlife; loud speakers are prohibited.
  • 🌉
    No Jumping or Diving: Jumping from bridges, dams, or trees is illegal and hazardous due to shallow limestone boulders.
✅ PERMITTED & REQUIRED
  • 🥤
    Reusable Containers Only: Insulated tumblers (Yeti, Hydro Flask), stainless steel bottles, or durable sports bottles (dishwasher-safe rule).
  • 🧊
    Coolers ≤ 30 Quarts: Allowed one locking/latching cooler per person. Must remain securely fastened while floating.
  • 🗑️
    Mesh Trash Bag: Keep one mesh trash bag tied securely to each tube stack to catch packaging and keep waters pristine.
  • 🦺
    Life Jackets Advised: Free-flowing river currents and Rio Vista chute require swimming confidence; life jackets strongly recommended.
  • 👟
    Secured Water Shoes: Wear strap-on sandals or water shoes to prevent foot injuries on slippery limestone and river rock.
🌿 ECO-STEWARDSHIP & PARK NAVIGATION
  • 🌾
    Texas Wild Rice Sanctuary: Endangered plant endemic only to the upper river. Float gently overhead; do not stand on grass beds.
  • 🗺️
    "Go Zones" vs. "No Zones": Disposable containers are permitted only in designated "Go Zones" (park picnic areas away from riverbanks).
  • 🐢
    Respect Native Wildlife: Admire basking turtles, herons, and river fauna from your tube without harassing or feeding.
  • 🏊
    No Lifeguards on Duty: The San Marcos River is a natural spring waterway with submerged roots and sudden drop-offs.
  • ⏰
    Park Hours (6 AM – 11 PM): River access parks close at 11:00 PM unless otherwise posted.
